strategy.summary: Reproduce the complex-NaN array_equivalent bug in pandas by building the buggy commit 61cbe5f9c92c from source (Cython extensions required) and running the developer's new parametrized test test_array_equivalent_complex_nan_component in pandas/tests/dtypes/test_missing.py; it should fail on the buggy revision (dtype_equal=True fastpath compares real and imaginary float components independently) and pass on the fixed revision (whole-element NA comparison).

system_packages: a C/C++ compiler toolchain (gcc or clang)
pinned_because: NumPy has no documented constraint and no era table entry, so it is left unpinned; the choice is the current NumPy 2.x release that the buggy commit builds against, not a value stated by the evidence.
python-dateutil, Cython and pytest are unbounded in the evidence; left unpinned by choice.
tzdata is documented only as required on Windows/Emscripten and is not needed on Linux.

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision 61cbe5f9c92c the parametrized test fails (at least the dtype_equal=True cases for c16/c8/>c16/>c8, where array_equivalent(np.array([1+nanj]), np.array([2+nanj]), dtype_equal=True) returns False instead of True); on the fixed revision (the PR #66323 change applied) all parametrized cases pass, with dtype_equal=True and dtype_equal=False agreeing.
strategy.numerical_probe: array_equivalent(np.array([1+np.nan*1j]), np.array([2+np.nan*1j]), dtype_equal=True) and the same with dtype_equal=False, compared for agreement.

input_output_examples.input: Series.equals on the same complex elements with NaN imaginary part and differing real parts

risks: The defect is in the dtype_equal=True fastpath for native complex; it is not platform-specific, so it should reproduce on Linux x86_64, but the buggy commit must be built from source with the Cython extensions so that the installed pandas matches the revision under test.

Non-native byte-swapped complex (>c16, >c8) is part of the test parametrization and is related to GH#65192 byte-swap reinterpretation; if the buggy revision already routes non-native dtypes away from the view path, those cases may pass on buggy and only the native c16/c8 cases will transition.

Related fixes GH#65192 and GH#66160 are unreleased in 3.1.0.dev, so the buggy commit cannot be substituted with a released pandas wheel; a released version either lacks the fix or differs in other ways.
Editable build requires a working compiler and Cython; a build failure on the buggy commit would prevent any transition.

Environment-specific NumPy/Python version combinations are not given by the evidence; a NumPy release that changes complex comparison or isnan behaviour could mask the bug, so pin to a NumPy that matches the repository's CI for that commit if the test does not transition.
The reproduction depends on pytest collecting only the new test; the -k filter must match the exact test name to avoid running unrelated tests.

oracle.reference_source: dtype_equal=False path in pandas array_equivalent, which uses (left == right) | (np.isnan(left) & np.isnan(right)).all()
oracle.why: Boolean equivalence result; the test asserts truth values of array_equivalent, so exact boolean agreement is the oracle.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On buggy 61cbe5f9c92c, the first assertion array_equivalent(left, right, dtype_equal=True) with left=[1+nanj] and right=[2+nanj] returns False because the fastpath compares the real parts (1 vs 2) independently of the NaN imaginary parts, so the assert fails for native c16 and c8 cases.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision, the element-wise NA comparison treats both elements as NA and returns True for the first assertion; the subsequent mixed and differing-finite assertions also hold, so all parametrized cases pass.
